findings.title: Computed Zod keys do not preserve expiry fields
findings.body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard key validator. The second computed property also overwrites the first, and z.object strips unrecognized properties. Consequently, synced responses lose expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other actual token fields. For example, Zoom computes its saved expiry from an undefined expires_in. Use an explicit response schema or a catchall/passthrough schema with a defined expiry contract.

findings.title: Google saves the safeParse result instead of credential data
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, but this code writes that entire wrapper into credential.key. This happens even when credential syncing is disabled. After the first successful refresh, the stored key no longer has access_token and other Google credential fields at its top level, so subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse it. Save the parsed data rather than the wrapper.

findings.title: Sync returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting SDK or Axios objects
findings.body: The sync branch returns an unparsed Fetch Response, whereas the fallback preserves each caller's native return shape. Google reads res.data, HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly, and Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data. None of these properties exists on a Fetch Response, so their synced refreshes throw or use undefined tokens even if the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize the response and adapt these callers to the same contract.

findings.title: Bigin sends a credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
findings.body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a userId, which is posted as calcomUserId to the parent application. Bigin instead passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs are independent, so the endpoint looks up the wrong user (or no user), and may return another user's credentials. Pass the credential's userId through to this method.

findings.title: New Salesforce persistence uses an unimported Prisma client
findings.body: The added prisma.credential.update call references prisma without importing or declaring it anywhere in this file. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError on every Salesforce client initialization after token refresh. Import the Prisma client before using it.

findings.title: Missing refresh tokens are replaced with an unusable literal
findings.body: This helper inserts the literal "refresh_token" whenever the response omits refresh_token, including when syncing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly allows omission, and its caller merges parsed data over the existing credential. The inserted literal therefore overwrites the valid stored refresh token, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.title: Zoom refresh uses a different app slug from credential installation
findings.body: The sync request sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials are installed with appId "zoom" and the webhook accepts the app-store slug. A parent app store looking up credentials using the supplied slug cannot match Zoom refresh requests to the installed app. Send "zoom", consistently with the callback and webhook contract.
